summary: This diff (commit 581e734) genuinely closes the 4 previously-rejected gaps: it wires query.py's NEEDS_OWNER_CLARIFICATION check into gateway.py's route_and_dispatch() before any submit/start/status dispatch (verified the gate reads the same on-disk chat record process_chat() just wrote, synchronously, in-process, so no race), fixes a real None-confidence TypeError/false-positive for document-mode chat records, gates start on submit's own duplicate_found signal (confirmed cmd_submit in task-gateway.py genuinely returns duplicate_found/duplicate_evidence), and adds a real --repo override checkpoint that is correctly threaded from the CLI flag through route_and_dispatch/dispatch_to_task_lifecycle into the actual start subprocess argv. The task-gateway.py change is comment-only (documenting that --repo was already wired to credit-accountant.py propose in a prior commit), which matches the commit message's framing as verification rather than a new fix. Ran the full test suite locally: 12/12 targeted tests and 23/23 full suite pass, matching the stated results. No shell/command-injection risk (all subprocess calls use argument lists), no .github/workflows/** changes, and no touched path matches the tier2 patterns (migrations/schema/auth/permission/payment/billing/rls/security), consistent with the pre-assigned tier1 classification. One pre-existing, out-of-scope issue noted below for a future follow-up but not a blocker for this PR.
issues: Pre-existing, unrelated to this diff: TaskGateway._save_chat_record()/get_chat_record() (scripts/prompt_gateway/gateway.py) hard-code the module-level CHATS_DIR constant instead of deriving a chats-dir from self.base_dir, even though __init__ derives data_dir/tags_dir/context_dir/snippets_dir from an explicit base_dir override. Chat records (including those written by tests that pass base_dir=tmp_path) always land in the real global CHATS_DIR, not the intended override path. This diff's new clarification gate still works correctly because both the writer (_save_chat_record) and reader (query.py's run_query) consistently use the same global path, but it means test runs leave real chat-record files behind outside tmp_path -- worth a small follow-up fix, not a reason to reject this PR.
